title: Part Three, Chapter 10: The Offerings to Tohil

verses.t: And this was the beginning and the decision to set Tohil there. And then they went before Tohil and Avilix; they went to see them and greet them and to give them thanks as well, because the dawn had come for them; and they danced before them, at the stone all pierced through, in the forest; and only by a miracle did it speak. And when those great ones came before Tohil, they brought nothing of value, only resin and rachacnoh (which is also a resin) and marigold, and this they burned before Tohil, their god. And then Tohil spoke, and only by a miracle did he speak, giving them direction, and the gods said: "Here shall be our homeland; we are yours. And so great is our fortune and greatness, through all the peoples who are ours, with all the peoples; and we are your companions on the road. Take care of your people, and we too shall teach them. Do not shame us before the people, when we grow angry at those words of theirs and the manner of their mouths. And so do not let us be caught in nets; give us only the straw and the scorned grass; and they will come only to give us the female deer and the females of the birds, and a little of their blood for us. Poor us! The deer's hide will be left behind. Guard against the sight of the eyes, against the deceits they will practise on them; and this shall be their deer, and these shall be our substitutes before the people. And when they say to you, 'Where is Tohil?', then show them the deer, and do not show yourselves; for there is something else to be done, since your being is great. And let all the peoples labour, and they will bring their blood before us; and embrace what is theirs." So said Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz; and they looked like young men when they came out and when the offering was brought before them. And then began the hunting of the young of the birds and of the deer; traps were set by the chiefs, and when they found the young birds and the tender deer and the females, they went and put the blood on the mouth of the stone of Tohil and Avilix; and when they brought the blood to the god, at once the stone would speak, when those lords came who brought it the offering. And likewise they did before the deer, burning resin, marigold and holomocox (which is an herb). And the deer [the men] were each on his own mountain, because they were pursued, and they did not live in their dwellings by day, but wandered through the forests, and ate only the grubs of hornets and wasps, and searched for honeycombs; and they had no good food or drink. And then nothing was known of their dwellings, and it is not known where their wives or women went about.
